name: Vdara Hotel & Spa
positioning: All-suite, casino-free and smoke-free spa hotel in CityCenter on the Las Vegas Strip, between Bellagio and Aria
best_for: Travelers who want Strip access but a calmer, casino-free and smoke-free place to stay
Longer stays and families who value suite space and kitchenettes

facts.text: Vdara is a casino-free, smoke-free spa resort on the Las Vegas Strip.
Vdara sits in the CityCenter complex between Bellagio and Aria, set slightly back from Las Vegas Boulevard.
Vdara opened in 2009 as part of CityCenter, conceived from the start as a condo-hotel hybrid.
Every room at Vdara is a suite.
Standard studios come with a sitting area, a dining table and a kitchenette with a cooktop, microwave, sink and refrigerator.
The look is modern and somewhat understated, more sleek condo than themed resort.
The naturally lit fitness center has cardio equipment with personal entertainment centers, weight machines and free weights.
Pedestrian paths and interior walkways connect Vdara to Aria, Bellagio and the wider CityCenter complex, including the Shops at Crystals.
T-Mobile Arena and Park MGM are an easy walk away for concerts and games.
Market Café Vdara handles quick breakfasts, salads, sandwiches and grab-and-go meals, plus groceries.
VICE VERSA Patio & Lounge is the hotel's main bar and social space, with indoor-outdoor seating.
Vdara is part of MGM Rewards.

highlights.text: The Spa at Vdara is spread across two floors, with European-style heat experiences, quiet relaxation areas and ESPA-branded treatments.
Vdara Pool & Cabanas has private retreats and cabanas with semi-secluded plunge pools.
Floor-to-ceiling windows frame views of the mountains, CityCenter or, in fountain view layouts, the Bellagio Fountains.
Larger suite categories add full kitchens and often in-suite washer-dryers, which make longer trips or work stays easier.
The pool deck is far more relaxed than the party scenes at many nearby properties, with no DJ-driven dayclub.

considerations.text: There is no casino at Vdara; guests walk over to Aria or Bellagio to play.
Vdara works well for families who value space and kitchenettes, but there is no dedicated kid zone.
WhataHotel notes a higher price point than traditional hotel rooms.
